details.description: Llama Guard 3 8B is Meta's content-safety classifier, fine-tuned from Llama 3.1 8B, that reads a prompt or a model's response and outputs a safety verdict plus which of 14 hazard categories it violates, following the MLCommons standardized hazard taxonomy. Released July 23, 2024, it is meant to run alongside a chat model as an input/output guardrail rather than as a general-purpose assistant, and adds detection for search-tool-call and code-interpreter abuse over Llama Guard 2. It classifies content in 8 languages: English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, and Thai.
advantages: Meta reports an English response-classification F1 of 0.939 with a 4.0% false positive rate on its internal MLCommons hazard-taxonomy test set, versus 0.877 F1 and an 8.1% false positive rate for Llama Guard 2, per the model card.
Meta reports an English prompt-classification F1 of 0.947 with a 5.7% false positive rate, per the model card.
Covers 14 hazard categories, including Code Interpreter Abuse (S14) added since Llama Guard 2, and is separately evaluated for search-tool-call abuse detection, per the model card.
Classifies content across 8 languages (English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Thai), per the model card.
Inherits a 131,072-token context window from its Llama 3.1 8B base, per Meta and Fireworks AI.
Meta also publishes an INT8-quantized build meant to lower deployment cost, per the model card.
disadvantages: Functions only as a safety classifier, not a general-purpose chat assistant.
Meta states hazard categories needing up-to-date factual knowledge, such as defamation and intellectual-property infringement, may need supplementary moderation systems, per the model card.
Meta notes the model can be susceptible to adversarial and prompt-injection attacks, per the model card.
use_cases: Screening user prompts before they reach a language model.
Screening model responses before they reach a user.
Flagging code-interpreter or search-tool-call abuse in agentic systems.

notes: Catalog's max_input/max_output_tokens (131072) match the 131K context window Meta and Fireworks AI report for this Llama-3.1-8B-based model, so no conflict. F1 is Meta's own 0-1 metric; multiplied by 100 here only to fit the catalog's 0-100 accuracy-score convention, it is not a literal accuracy percentage.
